answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. The beacon is the held bond, the pulse the tenure multiplier, and the marble the convex curve they ride; the beacon can be split but the pulse does not divide, and the marble punishes the split. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
